Accelerated Delivery Component of FCDO’s Tax Systems Transformation

Accelerated Delivery Component of FCDO’s Tax Systems Transformationprogramme (TSTP)

Technical assistance to support the transformation of Ethiopian tax systems required for a self-financed exit from poverty. Tax System Transformation Programme builds on existing UK support for tax systems reform, which the Government of Ethiopia has already adopted and implemented. Tax System Transformation Programme  will utilize and strengthen the delivery units already established within Ethiopian tax authorities, and draw heavily on centrally funded research.

To transform Ethiopia’s tax system so that the Ethiopian Government can fund more services for its population from its own revenues and become less dependent on aid. It takes an accelerated ‘delivery approach’ to tax reform that will generate at least £295million of additional tax revenue, reduce compliance costs for taxpayers, and support a better environment for businesses by improving clarity and the fairness of the tax system for businesses and investors. In doing so, it will create a platform for further sustainable increases in tax revenue and improve the Government's ability to assess the distributional impacts of its tax policies, particularly on the poor.

descriptions: Joint funding with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) - The IOM WASH program aims to improve access to adequate and equitable sanitation, and hygiene promotion for the Rohingya refugees, through sustainable WASH systems, community engagement, and emergency preparedness. This second FCDO grant will complement the ongoing FCDO project (June 2025 to March 2026). As such, it has been designed to address the additional infrastructure and NFI gaps in IOM camps, including soap to cover gaps in other camps under the area of responsibility of UNHCR and UNICEF. titles: Advancing Land-based Investment Governance (ALIGN)
descriptions: The goal of the Land Facility is to improve stability, inclusive growth and responsible investment by promoting more effective, efficient and equitable rural and urban land governance. Improved tenure security will contribute to a number of climate benefits; transformational change, reduced deforestation, increased resilience and sustainable land management practices. It will run for 7 years and will initially work in up to 10 countries in Africa and South East Asia depending on size and needs.

titles: Project Preparation for Strengthening Governance for Transformational Change in Water Security
descriptions:
This project preparation phase will develop a strong evidence-based multi-year strategy which supports strengthening governance and increasing investment in sustainable water use in land-based value chains to increase resilience and environmental benefits for people, nature, and climate. The project preparatory phase provides the opportunity to outline a coordinated approach for strategic alignment, integration, and connectivity of the three existing workstreams, and to ensure that through collaboration these workstreams are strengthened, scaled-up, and implemented in a coordinated manner. The main outcome of this period is the design of a multi-year work program which includes the Water Tracker, Resilient Water Accelerator, and Fair Water Footprint workstreams, and addresses the vision and objectives of the larger SGWC program. Over the course of the project preparatory period, partners from the three initiatives will work together to further define our strategic alignment, including in the following areas:

The most useful governance and project finance structures required to ensure strong and cost-effective delivery of the overall programme goal and the three areas of work.
Methods to maximize stakeholder and geographical alignment where appropriate and relevant for greatest impact.
How to embed monitoring, evaluation and learning both within and across the three programs, and within FCDO learning structures and processes, to effectively create a programme ‘learning cycle’.
How partnership across the consortia can support detecting, avoiding, and reducing potential risk factors across the programmatic areas.

This project preparatory phase will also include implementation of initiative specific activities under workstream, where those activities contribute to building the evidence base of the initiative individually, while also exploring further opportunities for alignment between the Water Tracker, RWA, and FWF.

titles: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning of Just Transitions for Water Security
descriptions:
The Just Transitions for Water Security Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) will independently review the performance and likely impact of the other four components namely the Water Resilience Tracker, Fair Water Footprints, Resilient Water Accelerator and Programme Management Support. It will also contribute to wider learning on ‘what works’.                                                                                                                    
 
The JTWS consortium will collaborate closely with The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning service provider engaged by the FCDO to support this programme of work. The MEL lead will be responsible for overseeing successful delivery of programme MEL, tracking impacts, and working with consortium partners to ensure a learning centred programme following FCDO’s best practice in adaptive management, and driven by the goal of transformative impact against a robust and well-tested theory of change. Engagement between the MEL service provider and the three workstreams will be coordinated through the Operational Coordination Unit (OCU) and Programme Executive Steering Committee (PESC). 

Progress towards the achievement of results will be monitored using the programme Theory of Change, the two programme-level ICF KPIs for resilience and transformational change and the four intermediate outcome level KPI’s (national integrated, inclusive, and water resilient climate strategies and plans, water security indices, stewardship standards met and investable plans). titles: Cash and food transfers to chronically food insecure households
descriptions: Ethiopia's rural safety net provides predictable cash and or food transfers to 8 million extremely poor people in chronically food insecure woredas (districts) in rural Ethiopia. Clients are selected for the program through a community-based targeting process. Households with able-bodied adult members are asked to work on community-planned public works in exchange for their transfers. These public works are activities like rehabilitate the natural resource base, build health posts and schoolrooms, construct and rehabilitate roads, and build other public infrastructure as prioritised by the community. Women are exempt from PW during pregnancy and 2 years postpartum. Labor-constrained households receive unconditional transfers (PDS) and are linked with complementary social services where possible. The safety net also provides livelihoods support in the form of skills training, business planning, savings promotion, credit facilitation, and, where appropriate, employment linkages.
